key_idea: Use three well-separated growth scales together with the structure theorem for transitive graphs, then split into cases. In the nilpotent case, finite percolation on a quotient group handles connectivity. In the isoperimetric case, many disjoint good subsets give each vertex a polylogarithmic-size cluster nearby, and stretched-exponential connection bounds glue these clusters together with a union bound.
reason: The strategy is sensible and expert-natural: reduce to a nilpotent quotient or to high-dimensional isoperimetry, then patch small and large orbit sizes. But the proof is dominated by bookkeeping of scales, absolute constants like 10^156, several sprinkling/coupling stages and a multi-case split. This makes it hard to hold in one's head, and it verifies the result more than it explains it.
recognized: Easo–Hutchcroft, 'Supercritical percolation on finite transitive graphs' (proof of the finite-graph p_c < 1 theorem)
